data.title: Shadow Sleuth: Decoding Time with Sun and Shadows
data.description: Investigate how the sun's changing position in the sky alters the direction and length of shadows, and use your detective skills to reverse-engineer the time of day just by looking at a shadow!

challenges.instruction: The shadow of the flagpole is very long and points toward the west (right). What time of day could this be?
challenges.hint: Remember that when the sun is low in the sky, shadows stretch out to their maximum length.

challenges.instruction: Look at the shadow cast by the flagpole. It is medium in length and still points toward the west (right). Can you determine the time?
challenges.hint: As the morning progresses and the sun climbs higher, shadows get shorter than they were at sunrise.

challenges.instruction: The shadow is very short and points directly north (below the object). What time is indicated by this position?
challenges.hint: When the sun reaches its highest point overhead, shadows are at their shortest.

challenges.instruction: The shadow has moved to the other side and is now medium in length, pointing toward the east (left). What time is it?
challenges.hint: Once the sun passes midday and moves toward the west, the shadows flip to point toward the east.

challenges.instruction: The shadow is very long and points sharply toward the east (left). Using your knowledge of the sun's path, identify the time.
challenges.hint: As the sun gets low in the western sky near the end of the day, shadows lengthen dramatically again.
